idealIf: You want manicured flower beds, a pond bridge and a warm glass greenhouse in one park, with frames that still work when the gardens go bare.
walkingNote: Flat paved paths through the gardens and around the pond. The ski hill sits at the far north end of the park.
permits: A City of Brampton permit is required for professional and wedding photography. Book through Facility Rentals at least four weeks ahead, with proof of $5 million liability insurance naming the City. The Tropical Gardens greenhouse opens 12 p.m. to 8 p.m. daily and books separately at its own rate.
permitFee: Outdoor Photo Permit: $85.60 per 60 minutes resident, $128.39 per 60 minutes non resident or commercial, plus HST. City of Brampton 2026 user fee schedule, effective January 1, 2026. Confirm which rate applies when you book.
permitContact: City of Brampton Facility Rentals. Chinguacousy Park bookings 905.458.6555. General rentals 905.874.2665 or facilityrentals@brampton.ca
parking: Free parking in the park lots on ordinary days. The lots off Central Park Drive sit closest to the gardens and greenhouse. The north end lot near the ski hill is about a 10 minute walk from the flower beds. Lots fill on summer weekends. A separate Canada Day parking fee is listed by the City.

name: Gage Park
vibe: heritage, downtown, bandstand, formal gardens, mature trees, nostalgic
vibeLine: Brampton's oldest park, opened in 1903, with a bandstand near its centre and mature trees breaking the late light across the flower beds.
idealIf: You want a small heritage park where a bandstand, a fountain and formal flower beds all sit within a two minute walk, plus a skating trail in winter.
walkingNote: Flat paved loops around the bandstand and gardens. A few steps where the ground rises toward Alderlea at the south end.
permits: Brampton requires a permit for professional photography and wedding ceremonies in its parks, booked through Facility Rentals. Requests made less than four weeks ahead may not be considered. Every rental needs $5 million liability insurance naming the City as an additional insured.
permitFee: $85.60 resident or $128.39 non resident and commercial, per 60 minutes, plus HST, per the 2026 City of Brampton user fee schedule effective January 1, 2026. Exclusive use of the gazebo is a separate $196.75 or $295.12 per 60 minutes. Insurance is quoted separately at booking.
permitContact: City of Brampton Recreation Facility Rentals, 905.874.BOOK (2665) or facilityrentals@brampton.ca
parking: Five municipal garages nearby, including City Hall at 2 Wellington Street West. Paid weekdays 9 am to 7 pm: first two hours free, then $1 per half hour to a $9 maximum. Free outside those hours, weekends and holidays. Nelson Square is free. Main Street closes Saturdays 6 am to 2 pm, June to October.

name: Heart Lake Conservation Park
vibe: Quiet, forested, lakeside, glacial, unhurried
vibeLine: A kettle lake the glaciers left behind, ringed by forest and planted pine rows, still enough most mornings to hold your reflection off the shore.
idealIf: You want water, forest, and real quiet away from downtown parks, and don't mind driving to Brampton or timing around family day use traffic near the beach.
walkingNote: Flat day use area by the lake, stairs down to the boathouse, natural surface trails beyond it
permits: TRCA has no published photo permit fee for Heart Lake and asks photographers to email Visitor Services first. Gate admission is paid per vehicle. Weddings and organized gatherings need a booked permit. Drones require TRCA authorization and are not allowed without it.
permitContact: TRCA Visitor Services
parking: Parking is included in the per vehicle gate fee, not billed separately, but a second car still pays full admission again. The 2026 passenger vehicle rate is $26.20 plus HST and the gate is cashless. Last admission is one hour before closing. Weekends only in fall, closed November through April.

name: Peel Art Gallery Museum and Archives (PAMA)
vibe: Historic, 1867 courthouse, jail complex, stone, heritage, cinematic
vibeLine: An 1867 county courthouse and jail in downtown Brampton, where the old courtroom and the heavy stone exterior sit a few steps apart.
idealIf: You want an 1867 courtroom and heavy heritage stone instead of another park, all inside one guided two hour session in downtown Brampton.
walkingNote: Accessible site. Ground level entrances, elevators to all floors, short flat walks between the buildings.
permits: PAMA books its own photo sessions, so there is no city permit. The wedding photoshoot is $360 plus tax for two hours, staff guided through the courthouse and exterior grounds, in opening hours only. Closing is 4:30 p.m. most days, 9 p.m. Thursday. No photos in the permanent galleries, no drones.
permitFee: $360 plus tax for a two hour wedding session
permitContact: pamadevelopment@peelregion.ca or 905-791-4055
parking: Limited onsite lot with three free accessible spaces, entered from the laneway between the buildings. The City Hall garage at 2 Wellington Street West is closest: first two hours free on weekdays, free on weekends and holidays. Street meters are $2 an hour, Monday to Saturday, 90 minute maximum.

name: Belfountain Conservation Area
vibe: Misty, storybook, heritage, forested, escarpment
vibeLine: The bridge sways a little when you cross it, the falls run right underneath, and the old stone fountain waits on the far bank.
idealIf: You want a waterfall, a swaying bridge and a historic cave in one small park, and you can work inside a two hour entry slot booked two weeks out.
walkingNote: Short accessible path to the bridge and fountain. Stairs and steeper grades on the gorge trails.
permits: Credit Valley Conservation requires a photography permit for professional photography and videography. Apply through the CVC photography, film and drone permit form. A timed entry reservation and a per vehicle permit are also required, and park admission is charged per person.
permitFee: $75 plus HST for a 2 hour permit, 2026 rate, plus park admission and the vehicle permit. One CVC page states the rate per hour, so confirm the duration when applying.
permitContact: Credit Valley Conservation photography, film and drone permit form; parks line 1-800-367-0890
parking: On site lot, vehicle permit $11.30 in 2026. Entry is by timed reservation only, bookable up to two weeks ahead with no same day slots. Walk in visitors are not permitted. The park opens for the season on Saturday April 25. Bookings are refundable only within 72 hours of booking.

name: Forks of the Credit Provincial Park
vibe: Rolling, open, wild, escarpment, cinematic
vibeLine: Rolling escarpment hills and a kettle lake minutes from the trailhead. The waterfall sits deeper in the gorge, and I think it's worth the walk.
idealIf: You want wide open Caledon hills and quiet kettle lake water instead of a city backdrop, and you don't mind booking a vehicle permit days in advance.
walkingNote: Kettle Lake is near the lot. Falls leg is long, hilly, with steps. Stay on marked trails. Meadow link closed.
permits: Ontario Parks publishes no photography permit here. Every vehicle needs a day use permit, bought in advance; booking opens at 7:00 a.m. five days ahead. Permits cover 8:00 a.m. to 10:00 p.m. only. The park map requires an application to the superintendent for filming, so clear paid shoots first.
permitContact: Park phone (705) 435-2498. Mail c/o Earl Rowe Provincial Park, PO Box 872, Alliston ON L9R 1W1. Ontario Parks lists 705-435-0847 for Park Superintendent arrangements at this park. The park map directs filming and research requests to the Superintendent.
parking: One designated gravel lot off McLaren Road with limited capacity, entered through an automatic gate that scans the permit barcode. The 2026 vehicle permit is $18.00 full day or $8.50 for four hours. Roadside parking, including Forks of the Credit Road, draws tickets and tows. Slots sell out.

name: Alton Mill Arts Centre
vibe: Stone mill, heritage industrial, artful, rustic, creekside, mill pond, cinematic
vibeLine: An 1881 stone knitting mill on Shaw's Creek, artist studios still working inside and the old mill pond lying quiet behind the walls.
idealIf: You want an 1881 stone mill, working artist studios, and creekside quiet in one place, and you do not mind an hour or more of driving into Caledon for it.
walkingNote: Level entrances and an interior lift. Courtyards are flat stone, creek and pond edges are uneven.
permits: Privately run heritage site that issues its own photography permits. Visiting and casual photos are free during public hours, Wednesday to Sunday, 10am to 5pm. Professional sessions need a permit arranged in advance. Wedding bookings include grounds access and one photo permit.
permitContact: info@altonmill.ca or 519-941-9300
parking: Free on-site lot with accessible spaces and four Level 2 EV chargers on the Flo network. The vehicle entrance is the driveway off Amelia Street, not Queen Street West. Street parking is available nearby. The site hosts festivals and open studio weekends that can affect parking.

name: Terra Cotta Conservation Area
area: Terra Cotta, Halton Hills near Caledon
vibe: Forested, escarpment, lake reflections, sugar maple, quiet
vibeLine: Wolf Lake and the sugar bush on one easy loop, a boardwalk over restored wetland, and the main Bruce Trail route climbing the escarpment behind it.
idealIf: You want quiet forest, a lake loop and a real escarpment climb in one session, and an hour of highway out of the city does not scare you.
walkingNote: Crushed stone loop and wetland boardwalk near the lot. The Escarpment Trail is a short steep climb.
permits: No permit is needed for personal photography. Credit Valley Conservation requires a professional photography permit for hired sessions, $75 plus HST. CVC pages disagree on whether that buys one hour or two and whether admission is included, so confirm the total. Drones are prohibited.
permitFee: $75 plus HST for a professional photography permit
permitContact: Credit Valley Conservation parks line 1-800-367-0890, permit form at cvc.ca/explore-activities/photography-filming/
parking: Onsite lots at 14452 Winston Churchill Blvd. No separate parking fee, admission is per person. 2026 rates: adult $8.50, youth $3.75, senior $6.75, under six free. Two EV chargers. Hours 8 a.m. to 8 p.m. daily, dropping to 8 a.m. to 7 p.m. on September 21, 2026. No entry 30 minutes before close.

name: Boyd Conservation Park
vibe: Forested, river valley, green, classic, unhurried
vibeLine: Old hemlocks, a steep valley, the East Humber running through it. I like that you park close and still shoot like you drove two hours north.
idealIf: You want deep valley forest and a river close to the city, with a short walk from the car so a long dress never has to cross a whole trail.
walkingNote: Park roads reach the valley trailheads; forest paths are packed dirt with roots and some valley approaches are steep
permits: No photography permit is published for Boyd. TRCA groups it with other conservation areas that require a direct email to Visitor Services at vservices@trca.ca for permit questions. Paid gate entry still applies, and TRCA requires a booked permit for an actual ceremony at the park.
permitContact: TRCA Visitor Services, vservices@trca.ca or 416-667-6295
parking: Parking is bundled into gate admission, billed per vehicle at $26.20 plus HST in 2026; a second vehicle pays the fee again. Online prepayment is available. Roads run about 1.5 km to the valley lots. Weekends only from late September, closed November through April, last entry an hour before close.

name: Kleinburg Village Main Street
vibe: Village charm, heritage buildings, small town, warm, walkable
vibeLine: Old village houses turned into shops line the east side of Islington Avenue, set close enough that one slow walk gives you several backdrops.
idealIf: You want small village warmth and heritage shopfronts about forty five minutes from downtown, instead of a long drive into the country.
walkingNote: Flat village sidewalks. Sidewalk sections close during the Kleinburg Village Improvements work on Islington Avenue.
permits: Commercial photography on City owned lands needs a permit under Vaughan By-law 169-2020, issued in one hour blocks that include setup. Vaughan publishes no rule for the Islington Avenue sidewalk, which is road allowance. Confirm with the City and apply at least 30 days ahead.
permitFee: $128.33 commercial and non Vaughan, or $106.94 resident, per one hour block before HST. City of Vaughan outdoor rate effective Jan. 1 to Dec. 31, 2026.
permitContact: City of Vaughan Recreation Services, rec@vaughan.ca. For sidewalk and road allowance questions, bylaw.licensing@vaughan.ca or 905-832-2281.
parking: Free unmarked on street spaces on Islington Avenue and Nashville Road, three hour limit 6 a.m. to 6 p.m. and none 2 a.m. to 6 a.m. Public lots at the Kleinburg Public Library and Pierre Berton Heritage Centre. Most core lots are private and signed customer only. Construction moves parking in 2026.

name: McMichael Canadian Art Collection
vibe: Group of Seven, woodland, hewn log and stone, sculpture garden, cinematic
vibeLine: One hundred acres of Group of Seven woodland around a hewn log gallery, bronze sculptures hiding along the paths, and a ridgetop over the Humber.
idealIf: You want the woods the Group of Seven painted, hewn log and fieldstone walls, and a quiet ridgetop, and you can shoot it before the gates close.
walkingNote: Woodland paths and a ridgetop hill. The paved entrance drive has no sidewalk.
permits: Posed wedding and engagement sessions on the grounds need a McMichael photo permit, 10 am to 4 pm. Each permit is a two hour block with up to 30 minutes per location. No drones anywhere on the property. Grounds permits run only through September 20, 2026, then depend on the construction timeline.
permitContact: photopermits@mcmichael.com
parking: Free on site lot via the security buzzer at the gate. Parking was $7 per vehicle before the gallery made it free until August 31, 2026. The rate since then is not published. En Plein Air Drive is a fire route. The city tickets parked cars there. Lot closes to vehicles once construction starts.

name: Eagles Nest Golf Club
vibe: Links style, rolling fairways, fescue rough, elegant, sunset views
vibeLine: A links style course of rolling fairways and fescue north of the city, with a lower patio built for outdoor ceremonies and sunset views.
idealIf: You want a links style golf course with rolling fairways and sunset views, on one property that holds the ceremony, the photos and the reception.
walkingNote: Clubhouse, lower patio and terrace are the main spaces. The venue lists transportation provided for photo locations.
permits: Eagles Nest is a public golf club on private property, so no city permit applies. Wedding and event photography is arranged inside the venue booking with the sales team. The club publishes no photography or drone policy for people who are not booked clients, so confirm access first.
permitContact: Eagles Nest sales team at sales@eaglesnestgolf.com or 905.417.2300
parking: Free parking on site, a short walk from the clubhouse, with reserved accessible spaces. The main entrance is on the west side of Dufferin Street just north of Major Mackenzie Drive. The golf course closes for the winter season, so outdoor course backdrops read spring through fall.

name: Copper Creek Golf Club
vibe: Copper roofed clubhouse, valley views, manicured, grand, polished
vibeLine: A copper roofed clubhouse above the Humber River Valley, with a stone gazebo and a terrace where the last hour of light runs long and gold.
idealIf: You want a valley view wedding venue, a stone gazebo ceremony, and a terrace that holds golden hour without leaving Vaughan.
walkingNote: Clubhouse, terrace, and gazebo sit close together, with stairs down to the lower terrace. Course views need a cart.
permits: Copper Creek is a privately run club, so access runs through its events office, not a city or conservation permit desk. No photography policy is published. Photography is documented only inside booked weddings and events. The course closes for the season in November while event spaces stay open.
permitContact: Copper Creek events office, 905.893.3370 ext 202
parking: On site surface parking sits beside the clubhouse, reached by the private drive from the Highway 27 gate. No fee, capacity, or public access statement is published, so treat it as parking for golf and event guests and confirm with the events office. No street parking is published on Highway 27.

name: The Doctor's House
vibe: Historic, chapel, garden, village charm, intimate
walkingNote: Chapel connects indoors to the event rooms and an accessibility elevator serves the levels. Gardens and patios on site.
permits: Private property, so Vaughan's commercial photography by law for City owned lands does not apply here. Photography happens inside a booked event or ceremony. The preferred vendor list names only an officiant, audio and pianist, so no photographer is required. Confirm other sessions with sales.
permitContact: The Doctor's House sales team, TDHSales@thedoctorshouse.ca or 905-893-1615
parking: On site surface lots front and back, roughly 208 spaces per city studies, shared with the XXI Chophouse restaurant and up to three events during restaurant hours. Both lots get busy from about 4:30pm and valet is sometimes offered. Village street parking is three hours, 6am to 6pm.
idealIf: You want a chapel ceremony and garden portraits on one property, with the reception a short indoor walk away and nobody moving a car.
vibeLine: A wooden pew chapel with cathedral windows and its own bell, set in the gardens of a 19th century Kleinburg house that backs onto the Humber.

name: Main Street Unionville
vibe: Heritage, village, storybook, walkable, nostalgic
vibeLine: Painted 1800s shopfronts, a bandstand on the corner, Toogood Pond just north. I walk this whole street slowly and it never runs out of frames.
idealIf: You want a small village feel instead of a park, with heritage shopfronts along one street and Toogood Pond about ten minutes north on foot.
walkingNote: Flat sidewalks the length of the strip. Toogood Pond adds a short trail walk, but part of that trail is closed.
permits: Main Street Unionville is one of seven photography permit locations the City of Markham lists, booked through the Clerk's Office or the City's PerfectMind portal to reserve the spot for exclusive use. The by-law wording covers wedding photography. There is no separate Unionville BIA permit.
permitFee: $158.50 per permit plus HST under Markham's 2026 user fee by-law 2025-125. The City website separately lists $172.89 per hour, so confirm the basis with the Clerk before quoting.
permitContact: City of Markham Clerk's Office, clerks@markham.ca, 905.475.4744
parking: Free lots sit behind the Main Street businesses, entered off Carlton Road and Main Street Unionville, plus a free Toogood Pond lot at 218 Carlton Road. No maximum stay is published, so posted signs govern. Several event days close Main Street, so check the BIA events calendar.

name: Toogood Pond Park
vibe: Serene, pond, willows, boardwalk, village calm
vibeLine: Willows along the shoreline, a boardwalk through the cattails, and Unionville's heritage Main Street a short walk from the north entrance.
idealIf: You want a short, flat pond loop with willows and boardwalk in one frame, and a heritage village street nearby to finish the session on.
walkingNote: Flat loop, roughly 1.5 km, one bridge and a boardwalk. Pond mostly drained and paths closed for 2026 dam repairs.
permits: Toogood Pond is one of seven Markham sites that sell a photography permit. By-law 167-92 requires one for wedding photography in any Markham park. Engagement and portrait sessions are not addressed in writing. The by-law also bars park entry between midnight and 6 a.m. Book via the Clerk's Office.
permitFee: By-law 2025-125 lists a Wedding Photography Permit at $158.50 per permit plus HST, about $179.11. The City website lists $172.89 per hour. Confirm the basis with the Clerk's Office before quoting a client.
permitContact: City of Markham Clerk's Office, clerks@markham.ca, 905.475.4744
parking: Two small lots. The north entrance off Main Street Unionville sits beside the gazebo and the Boathouse washrooms. A second lot is off Carlton Road at the south end near the dam. The City publishes no fee or hours for either. Confirm access first, as 2026 dam and boardwalk repairs close paths.

name: Milne Dam Conservation Park
area: Markham, Rouge River valley off McCowan Road
vibe: Rural, riverside, wooded, meadow, quiet
vibeLine: I come out here for the wide water and the meadow grass, thick woods on the far bank and an old dam at the end of the trail.
idealIf: You want wide river light, meadow grass and deep woods in one quiet park, and you do not mind driving out to Markham for an afternoon with me.
walkingNote: Flat gravel and grass paths from the lots. The dam is about 1.5 km east, roughly 30 to 45 minutes on foot.
permits: No photography permit is sold for Milne Dam. The 1992 Markham parks bylaw requires a Town permit for wedding photography in any park, but the City sells permits for only seven other locations. Vehicle admission is charged per vehicle on weekends and statutory holidays, and is free on weekdays.
permitContact: City of Markham, 905.477.7000 (ask for the Clerk's Office about the parks bylaw), or rentalpermits@markham.ca for the park itself
parking: Free lots at 8251 McCowan Road, through a front gate. Open seasonally, roughly mid May to mid October, 9 AM to dusk on weekdays. Weekends and statutory holidays cost about $12 to $12.50 per vehicle, charged per vehicle so two cars pay twice. Weekdays are free. Credit or debit only, no cash.

name: Markham Museum
vibe: Rustic, heritage, pastoral, nostalgic, quiet
vibeLine: More than twenty heritage buildings spread over 25 acres, gravel lanes and open fields, and an 1848 church standing at the quiet end.
idealIf: You want 19th century brick, a bandstand and open field light in one booking, and you would rather shoot somewhere nobody else in your feed has used.
walkingNote: Flat grass and gravel paths across 25 acres. Heritage building interiors open only on guided tours.
permits: A photography permit is required for all photos taken on site except casual day out photos, so engagement and wedding sessions always need one. The permit covers two hours on the exterior grounds with a staff member guiding the session. Indoor venues are booked separately and are not guaranteed.
permitFee: Listed in the City of Markham user fee schedule as Wedding Photos External Only, $156.00 for two hours or $110.00 per hour, taxes and insurance extra. No separate engagement session rate is published.
permitContact: Markham Museum at museuminfo@markham.ca or 905.305.5970
parking: On site lot at 9350 Markham Road. The museum directs visitors to the northern end of the lot, to the right of the Mount Joy Administrative Building. Accessible spaces sit in front of the John Lunau Centre doors. No parking charge is posted. The site closes on some dates for private events.

name: Cathedral of the Transfiguration
vibe: Monumental, Byzantine, gold domes, symmetrical, cinematic
vibeLine: Three gold onion domes over an open plaza in Markham. I shoot it wide, because the building is the whole point.
idealIf: You want scale. A 210 foot gold tower, a stone Byzantine facade, and the two of you standing small and deliberate in the middle of it.
walkingNote: Flat paved plaza wraps the building. A short flight of steps leads up to the main doors.
permits: Private property, administered by the Slovak Greek Catholic Church Foundation. No photography policy is published. The open grounds are walkable, with no fee reported for casual photos, though this is not official. Organized sessions and ceremonies go through Jesus the King Melkite parish.
permitContact: Jesus the King parish office, 905.886.0700
parking: Free street parking on the Cathedraltown roads that ring the site. No official visitor lot is documented for the grounds. Three liturgies run on Sunday, so it is busiest then. The vacant land next door is a stalled development site, and the city bans street parking during winter snow clearing.

name: Mill Pond Park
area: Richmond Hill, corner of Mill Street and Trench Street
vibe: Tranquil, pond, footbridges, boardwalk, gazebo, heritage village
vibeLine: A quiet mill pond in old Richmond Hill, ringed by a trail and footbridges, with a boardwalk and a large gazebo on the south shore.
idealIf: You want still water, a gazebo and a footbridge in frame, and you would rather drive north for a calm setting than shoot downtown.
walkingNote: Flat paved paths and a boardwalk by the gazebo. York Region rates the 2.4 km pond trail easy.
permits: Park Use By-law 19-22 requires a City photo permit for wedding, engagement or any paid shoot. Two hour permits are sold May to October through the online Photo Permit Request form. Moving video and drones each need a separate permit. Parks close 11:30 p.m. to 7 a.m.
permitFee: $96.34 resident or $149.60 non resident, two hour permit, plus HST. The City publishes no effective date, so confirm the rate when booking.
permitContact: City of Richmond Hill online Photo Permit Request form; access@richmondhill.ca or 905-771-8800
parking: Two free City lots on the south side of Mill Street hold 50 spaces combined, two accessible in each. About 141 on street spaces sit nearby, capped at three hours by city by-law. The City parking study found both lots full during Concerts in the Park.

name: Richmond Green Park
area: Richmond Hill, Elgin Mills and Leslie
vibe: Manicured, garden, waterfall, heritage, unhurried
vibeLine: A gazebo on the pond, a rose garden, and a waterfall under an arched bridge, all close enough to shoot in one unhurried loop.
idealIf: You want a gazebo, a rose garden and a waterfall inside one easy walk, and you are fine buying the City permit the by-law requires.
walkingNote: Walkways link the gazebo, pond, waterfall and boardwalk, all within a few minutes on foot
permits: By-law 19-22 requires a permit to photograph a wedding or event, and to practise a profession, in any City park. Richmond Green is one of six permit locations. The permit page says May to October, the park page says May to September, so confirm the month. Parks open at 7 a.m.
permitFee: $96.34 resident or $149.60 non resident, per two hour permit, as published by the City
permitContact: Photo Permit Request form at forms.richmondhill.ca, or access@richmondhill.ca and 905-771-8800. The City replies within five business days.
parking: On site lots off Elgin Mills Road East, a short walk from the gardens. The City publishes no parking rate for this park, so confirm before counting on free parking. By-law 19-22 allows parking only in marked lots. Canada Day on July 1 and Ribfest both fill the park.

name: Phyllis Rawlinson Park
vibe: Pastoral, heritage, rural, open, unhurried
vibeLine: A farmhouse from about 1830 and its barn, York Region's oldest designated buildings, with moraine woodland behind them. I shoot the last light here.
idealIf: You want heritage farm buildings and quiet moraine parkland instead of a downtown block, and you do not mind driving north with me for softer light.
walkingNote: Short, flat walk from the parking area to the farmhouse and barn. York Region rates the 3.4 km trail network easy.
permits: City of Richmond Hill photo permit required for photographs taken in association with a wedding or other event in its parks, under Park Use By-law 19-22. Phyllis Rawlinson is one of six parks listed. Permits are listed as available May to October. The City aims to reply within 5 business days.
permitFee: $96.34 resident or $149.60 non resident for a two hour permit
permitContact: City of Richmond Hill Photo Permit Request form, or Richmond Hill Municipal Offices at access@richmondhill.ca and 905-771-8800
parking: Parking on site at the 11715 Leslie Street access point, listed by the City as a park amenity. No parking fee is posted here, and the City posts pay parking only at Lake Wilcox Park. Lot size is not published. York Region is rebuilding 19th Avenue into summer 2027.

name: Richmond Hill Heritage Centre
vibe: Historic, Regency cottage, landscaped gardens, white gazebo, intimate
vibeLine: An 1840 Regency cottage with a white gazebo on landscaped grounds behind it, a small park that can be worked end to end inside one permit block.
idealIf: You want an intimate heritage garden rather than a sprawling park, with a white gazebo and an 1840 Regency cottage in almost every frame.
walkingNote: Small flat park with short walking distances. The Heritage Centre building is fully wheelchair accessible.
permits: City of Richmond Hill photography permit required. Amos Wright Park is one of six eligible parks. Two hour permit, available May to October, requested through the online Photo Permit Request form. The City responds within five business days. A ceremony is a separate booking.
permitFee: $96.34 resident or $149.60 commercial and non resident, two hour permit, HST included, in effect until December 31, 2026
permitContact: Photo Permit Request form at forms.richmondhill.ca, or access@richmondhill.ca, 905 771 8800
parking: No parking is published on the Heritage Centre or Amos Wright Park pages. A City news item for a one day event pointed visitors to the Elgin Barrow Arena lot at 43 Church Street South, about 250 m away across Major Mackenzie Drive East. Cost and availability are unconfirmed.

name: Gairloch Gardens
vibe: lakefront estate, heritage, rose garden, manicured, serene, cinematic
vibeLine: A Tudor stone house above Lake Ontario, with rose beds and a pond on the slope below it and open water at the foot of the lawn.
idealIf: You want a lakefront estate look, roses and still water in one frame and open lake in the next, and you can book the permit weeks ahead.
walkingNote: Paved and gravel paths over rolling lawn that slopes to the lakeshore, with some steps and uneven ground.
permits: A Town of Oakville photography permit is required. Sessions are 90 minutes, start on the hour between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m., and book 45 to 4 days ahead. Cancel in writing 14 days ahead for a refund. Sessions run rain or shine. No indoor or washroom access. Confirm the current fee when booking.
permitContact: Town of Oakville Facility Bookings, bookafacility@oakville.ca or 905-815-2000
parking: Free town lot off Lakeshore Road East, about 35 spaces shared with gallery visitors. Parking cannot be guaranteed, so arrive early on summer weekends. Parks are open 6 a.m. to 10 p.m. Park in designated areas only, never on grass. Limousine parking is prohibited.

name: Erchless Estate
vibe: Historic, harbourfront, stately, garden estate, intimate
vibeLine: The founding family's 1858 house above Oakville Harbour, with broad lawns, stone walls, a 1920s rock garden and stairs down to Sixteen Mile Creek.
idealIf: You want a historic house, stone walls and harbour views in one small walkable estate, and you are fine booking a fixed 90 minute window weeks ahead.
walkingNote: Level lawns and a gravel drive around the house, then stairs or a sloping lawn down the bank to Sixteen Mile Creek.
permits: Advance online reservation required. No wedding ceremonies, and no access to indoor facilities or washrooms. Sessions are 90 minutes starting on the hour, 8 a.m. to 8 p.m., arrival and departure included. Book 4 to 45 days ahead. Rain or shine. Cancel in writing 14 days ahead for a refund.
permitFee: $331.20 plus HST resident, $412.97 plus HST non resident, per 90 minute session in the Town's 2026 rates schedule. The Photography in Parks page still lists $320 plus HST, so confirm the rate when booking.
permitContact: Facility Bookings, bookafacility@oakville.ca or 905-815-2000
parking: Limited free visitor parking beside the museum, listed as 12 spaces, and the Town says it cannot be guaranteed. Vehicles must stay in designated areas and limousines are prohibited. Navy Street meters are $2.50 per hour, three hour limit, free after 6 p.m. and Sundays. Downtown lots are $2 per hour.

name: Bronte Heritage Waterfront Park
vibe: Harbour, nautical, breezy, lakefront, unhurried
vibeLine: Masts and fishing boats along the harbour wall, a short pier out to the lighthouse, and the lake wide open behind it.
idealIf: You want a working harbour, a lighthouse at the end of the pier, and late lake light coming in over the boats.
walkingNote: Flat paved promenade and lawn. The short pier out to the lighthouse can close in high wind or heavy waves.
permits: Bronte is not on the Town of Oakville list of parks that require a photography permit, so open parkland shoots do not need one. A permit is required for a ceremony or booking at the Bronte Butterfly Gazebo. Commercial video may fall under a separate Town film permit.
permitFee: Butterfly Gazebo wedding ceremony booking, a two hour slot: $115 plus HST for residents, $163 plus HST for non residents. This matches the current 2026 Town rate schedule. No published fee covers casual photography or video elsewhere in the open park.
permitContact: Special Events, events@oakville.ca or 905-845-6601. Facility Bookings, bookafacility@oakville.ca or 905-815-2000
parking: Town lot at the park, 212 spaces, off Ontario Street just west of Bronte Road, signed Green P. The Town's page says parking is free until September 15 with no year given. That date just passed with no posted rate after it, so budget for paid parking. Fills early on summer weekends.

name: Coronation Park
vibe: Lakefront, breezy, open lawns, mature shade trees, easygoing
vibeLine: A wide pebble beach open to Lake Ontario, with mature shade trees and long lawns holding soft light just behind it.
idealIf: You want open water and big shade trees in one session, with a flat easy walk between them so nobody is fighting a hem or a heel.
walkingNote: Flat paved lakefront path and level lawns. The beach itself is loose pebbles and uneven underfoot.
permits: Coronation Park is not on Oakville's photography permit list, which names only Gairloch Gardens, Erchless Estate and the Butterfly Gazebo. Personal photos need no permit. The Destination Parks policy notes a permit may apply for ceremonies or paid photography. The five picnic areas book separately.
permitContact: Town of Oakville Facility Bookings, bookafacility@oakville.ca or 905-815-2000. For filming inquiries, Town Hall at 905-845-6601.
parking: Free town lot, 221 marked spaces across entrances at the east and west ends off Lakeshore Road West. No meters and no fee. Spaces fill fast on summer weekends and splash pad afternoons, so a weekday or an early golden hour is safer. Washrooms and the snack bar close for winter.

name: Graydon Hall Manor
vibe: Formal, historic, manicured, grand, estate
walkingNote: Flat terrace and lawns. Garden steps run down the slope, and a grand staircase leads to the upper level.
permits: Private venue on private grounds. Photography happens inside a booked event, or under a photo permit from the manor. The venue states it does not offer photo permits in peak season, May to October, and that photo bookings may be available November to April, subject to availability.
permitContact: Graydon Hall Manor at 416.449.5432
parking: On site parking for 120 cars, per the venue. The entrance is at 185 Graydon Hall Drive. The venue states it is available only for special events, so the lot serves booked events and approved photo bookings. No public rate is published. Surrounding streets are residential, so check posted signs.
idealIf: You want Georgian manor grandeur and formal gardens on your booked date, with a 160 foot terrace above the fountains to shoot end to end.
vibeLine: A 1936 fieldstone manor on the brow of a hill, its 160 foot stone terrace looking down over fountains and formal gardens.

name: Paletta Lakefront Park and Mansion
vibe: Heritage estate, wooded creek, lakefront lawns, quiet, cinematic
vibeLine: An estate house on fourteen acres of Burlington lakefront, a wooded creek folded in behind it and Lake Ontario at the end of the lawn.
idealIf: You want old estate grounds, a wooded creek and open lake in one short walk, and your date falls on a weekday when the park issues photo permits.
walkingNote: Flat lawns and a paved path by the mansion. Creek trails add dirt paths, short valley slopes and bridge steps.
permits: City of Burlington photography contract required, Monday to Thursday only, covering the north and south bridges. Booking season runs May 9 to Oct 4, in 90 minute blocks to a 3 hour maximum. Contracts do not guarantee exclusive use. Weekend terrace access is arranged through Edge Hospitality.
permitFee: $106.50 standard or $149.00 commercial and non resident, per 90 minute block plus HST
permitContact: City of Burlington rentals at rentals@burlington.ca or 905-335-7738; weekend terrace through Edge Hospitality at 905-632-7809
parking: On site lot off Lakeshore Road beside the mansion. Visitor guides report free parking but no current city page confirms it. Spaces are limited and the lot fills with wedding and banquet guests on weekends and in summer. The park is closed between 11 p.m. and 7 a.m.

name: LaSalle Park
vibe: Sheltered bay, heritage pavilion, marina masts, wooded shore, unhurried
walkingNote: Flat paved paths near the pavilion. The marina and shoreline sit downhill and some shore trails are unpaved.
permits: City of Burlington requires a booked group photography contract. LaSalle is one of five eligible parks. No photography season window is published, so check the Live and Play calendar. The pavilion cannot be booked, permits cover set spaces only, and the contract is not exclusive.
permitFee: $106.50 standard or $149.00 on the combined commercial and non resident tier, per 90 minute block plus HST. 2026 rate effective Apr 1. Maximum 2 consecutive blocks.
permitContact: rentals@burlington.ca or 905-335-7738, booked through the City of Burlington Live and Play system
parking: On site lots off LaSalle Park Road, an upper lot and a lower lot at the marina. The City publishes no car parking fee here but does not state that car parking is free, so check posted signs. The $20 daily HONK fee at the boat launch applies to boat trailers only. Lots fill fast on summer weekends.
idealIf: You want sheltered bay water instead of open lake chop, plus a 1917 pavilion, marina masts and a wooded shore inside one loop I can walk in an hour.
vibeLine: A sheltered bay on Burlington's Aldershot side, a 1917 pavilion above the water, and masts clinking at the marina a short walk down the slope.

name: Albion Falls
vibe: Tiered, cascading, forested, escarpment, dramatic
vibeLine: Red Hill Creek steps down the escarpment in wide shelves, loud in spring and gold in October, and you hear it before you clear the parking lot.
idealIf: You want a wide tiered waterfall behind you with almost no walking, and you are fine working from the platforms instead of down at the water.
walkingNote: Paved path about 200 metres from the Mountain Brow lot to the north viewing platforms. Wheelchair accessible.
permits: No standard City photo permit exists for ordinary shoots, so none can be bought here. Shooting is limited to the marked trails and north viewing platforms. Going past the fences or down to the base can draw a fine of $75 to $135 for entering a restricted area. Ten or more people need a City permit.
permitContact: Hamilton Film Office at film@hamilton.ca
parking: Three City lots with no posted parking fee. Closest lot is off Mountain Brow Boulevard beside the north platforms, plus Arbour Road and the Red Hill Valley trail lot on Mud Street. Lots fill early on weekends and during fall colour. Roadside parking is ticketed. Park hours are 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.

name: Princess Point
vibe: Marsh edge, wild, open water, prairie grass, quiet
vibeLine: A low sand point where Cootes Paradise opens up to the west, tall prairie grass at your backs and the whole marsh holding the last of the light.
idealIf: You want wild marsh and prairie grass instead of manicured garden beds, and a sunset that lands straight across open water.
walkingNote: Short flat walk from the lot to the shoreline loop. The wider trail network is hilly.
permits: Royal Botanical Gardens land, not a City of Hamilton park. RBG requires a permit for any professional session but sells permits only for Hendrie Park, the Rock Garden and the Arboretum. Princess Point is not a bookable permit location, so call RBG before booking a paid shoot there.
permitContact: Royal Botanical Gardens, 905-527-1158 ext. 285
parking: Paid RBG lot at 335 Longwood Road N, $3 per hour per vehicle to a $15 daily maximum in 2026. Overflow at the Westdale lot, 85 Oak Knoll Dr, same rate. RBG members park free. Trailheads open 8 a.m. to dusk. Winter skating days bring a staffed flat rate and a lot that fills early.

name: Sam Lawrence Park
vibe: Panoramic, elevated, skyline, breezy, display gardens
vibeLine: A stone lookout on the escarpment brow where the lower city, the harbour and Lake Ontario all open up behind you at golden hour.
idealIf: You want Hamilton's skyline and harbour behind you at sunset, with the display gardens and a flagpole lookout inside one short walk.
walkingNote: Paved paths with a moderate slope and a few stairs between levels. The lookout is flat from the west lot.
permits: City by-law bans running a business in a park without a permit, which can include paid photo shoots, backed by a $75 penalty. A 2026 fee schedule lists a wedding or photo booking fee at some parks, amount unconfirmed here. Call before booking. Default hours are 6 a.m. to 11 p.m.
permitContact: Hamilton Recreation (park permits), 905-546-3747 option 2. Hamilton Film Office (filming events), film@hamilton.ca, 905-546-4233.
parking: Two small free lots off Concession Street, a west lot near the main lookout and an east lot near the display gardens and pavilion. Both fill fast at sunset and on summer weekends, so arrive early. Free street parking along Concession Street is the usual overflow. No paid municipal lot on site.

name: Parkwood National Historic Site
vibe: Grand estate, formal gardens, heritage, stately, cinematic
vibeLine: A 1917 auto baron's mansion in Oshawa, eleven acres of heritage gardens around it, fountains and mature evergreens that hold light late in the day.
idealIf: You want auto baron grandeur and formal gardens, and you do not mind booking a paid photo pass and sharing the grounds with whoever else is booked.
walkingNote: Paved, flagstone, gravel and grass with surface changes. The far fountain end is a five minute walk from the lot.
permits: Casual phone or small camera photos are free. A photo pass is required for a professional camera, a hired photographer or an outfit change, and must be booked in advance. Outdoor is $300 plus HST for two hours, up to 20 people. Indoor is $400 plus HST, max 10. No drones. Grounds close in winter.
permitFee: $300 plus HST outdoor and $400 plus HST indoor, base rates published for 2026
permitContact: photos.weddings@parkwoodestate.com or 905-433-4311 ext. 32872
parking: Free on site parking for Parkwood guests, very limited and not guaranteed, designated areas only. Posted hours are 9am to 5pm Monday to Friday and 1pm to 5pm Saturday and Sunday, the same as the garden hours, with exceptions posted on the site banner. A paid garage sits west of the estate.

name: Lakeview Park
vibe: Lakefront, sandy, heritage, breezy, unhurried
vibeLine: A sand beach, a pier running out into Lake Ontario, and three nineteenth century heritage houses a short walk back from the water.
idealIf: You want open lake light and a long pier, then a short walk inland to three heritage houses for a completely different second look.
walkingNote: Flat paved paths link the heritage houses, beach and pier. Soft sand on the beach and a boardwalk at the beach access.
permits: City of Oshawa requires a Facility Booking Office permit for weddings or formal photos in any City park. The Photos in all City Parks line is $65 plus H.S.T. The City page lists rates per hour, the fees by law groups it under flat rate, so confirm basis. A permit grants access, not exclusive use.
permitFee: $65 plus H.S.T. for photos in all City Parks, 2026 rate. Per hour or flat rate basis not confirmed
permitContact: City of Oshawa Facility Booking Office, fbo@oshawa.ca
parking: Paid parking runs May 15 to October 15 on weekends, public holidays and City event days at $20 per vehicle per day for non residents, paid at on site meters or by HonkMobile. Free at other times. Resident permits need an Oshawa address. On Canada Day only M.T.O. accessible permit holders may park.

name: Oshawa Valley Botanical Gardens
vibe: Floral, peaceful, valley, creekside, unhurried
vibeLine: In June this creek valley fills with more than three hundred varieties of peonies, and the Memory Garden walkways lead to a pergola given by the Rotary Clubs.
idealIf: You want peonies in June, lilacs in late May, or a quiet fall valley, and you like that most Toronto couples never think to drive this far east.
walkingNote: Paved walkways, gentle slopes, one creek footbridge. No public washrooms. Closes 10 p.m. Apr to Oct, 6 p.m. Nov to Mar.
permits: City of Oshawa requires a permit for a wedding or formal photos on special occasions in its parks. Apply to the Facility Booking Office. A permit grants approval, not exclusive rights, so other permitted groups may share the area. A firefighters memorial is planned in the Memory Garden in 2026.
permitFee: $65 for photos in a City park and $131 when the ceremony is held on site, plus H.S.T. Fees do not include insurance. City pages call these hourly, while Fees and Charges By-law 109-2024 Schedule B lists them under a flat rate heading, so confirm the basis with the Facility Booking Office.
permitContact: City of Oshawa Facility Booking Office, fbo@oshawa.ca, 905-436-3311
parking: Lot at the Children's Arena, 155 Arena St. The City publishes no space count, fee or time limit for it, so check posted signs. On Peony Festival weekend that lot is Accessible Parking Permit only, nearby streets go local traffic only, and free off site lots run a shuttle.
